answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a stake in a vault before it may place orders, then slash that stake when an identity is proven to have double-spent or violated a signed commitment. Creating many names is still cheap, but making them economically useful is not: the attacker must fund every account, and coordinated misconduct risks losing the locked capital. As a tide of new identities reaches the wharf, the stake requirement makes a Sybil attack costly rather than impossible.
